title: World Orb and MPC technical authority depth 1
summary: Request #2095 resolves the public uniqueness architecture one layer deeper: iris-code inference is open, matching uses a three-party MPC design with an honest-majority assumption, Face Authentication stays local to the phone, and production MPC operator identities and governance remain unresolved.

gaps: Production identities and legal operators for all three iris-MPC parties remain unresolved.
Operator replacement, certificate rotation, persistence, backup and deletion authority remain unresolved.

data.question: What do current primary technical sources establish about iris-code generation, uniqueness matching, Face Authentication, and production MPC authority?
data.method: Reconciled current World developer documentation with the public open-iris, iris-mpc, MPC uniqueness-check and World ID protocol repositories.
data.framework: Raw images, iris-code inference, secret-shared uniqueness matching, on-device Face Authentication and production operator governance remain separate evidence layers.
data.scope: Orb iris-code generation, three-party MPC uniqueness architecture, security assumptions, Face Authentication and unresolved production operator authority.
findings: World's open-iris repository documents an iris-recognition pipeline that converts iris imagery into iris codes and can run in an Orb environment.
The public MPC uniqueness-check repository describes SMPC used to calculate fractional Hamming distance for iris-code uniqueness matching.

The current iris-mpc repository states that both GPU and CPU implementations assume three participating parties, semi-honest execution and an honest majority, meaning at most one party may be adversarial without collusion.
Current World developer documentation describes matching as split across independent nodes so no single party holds complete sensitive matching data.

World Face Authentication documentation says encrypted face images used for authentication are stored on the user's phone and comparison occurs locally; TFH and World Foundation do not receive a copy through that path.
The reviewed public sources do not identify all current production legal entities operating the three MPC parties or who can replace, reconfigure, suspend or coordinate them.
conclusions: The reviewed iris-MPC privacy model depends on secret sharing plus a three-party honest-majority and no-collusion assumption.
Face Authentication is a separate local-device path and should not be conflated with iris uniqueness matching.
The next control question is who operates each production MPC party and who has authority to replace or reconfigure those parties.
recommendations: Recover production MPC operator identities, hosting providers, jurisdictions, deployment manifests and contractual independence requirements.
Recover party rotation, certificate replacement, incident response, backup and deletion controls.
Reconcile production deployment evidence with regulator findings before making claims about operational independence or deletion.
counterarguments: Open-source architecture does not prove production operators are organizationally independent.
Secret-shared biometric-derived material does not imply one MPC party can reconstruct a usable iris template under the stated model.
limitations: No private production infrastructure or private user biometric data was accessed.
Operator identities were not inferred from cloud names or repository examples.
unresolved: Which legal entities operate the three production iris-MPC parties today?
Who can rotate certificates, replace a party or suspend matching?
What persistence, backup and deletion controls apply to secret-shared iris material?

methods: primary technical documentation and source-repository review

data.research_question: What can current primary technical sources establish about World Orb uniqueness matching and the authority boundary of its MPC architecture?
data.method: Extended the existing request-2095 packet with primary World technical sources without duplicating existing identities.
classification_rules: Open-source design is not proof of production deployment.
Cryptographic party separation is not proof of organizational independence.
Face Authentication local storage is distinct from iris uniqueness matching.
A security assumption is recorded as an assumption, not a guaranteed operational fact.

findings.finding: Public iris-MPC code uses a three-party semi-honest honest-majority model and assumes no collusion by two parties.
World documentation describes matching as distributed across independent nodes while the reviewed sources do not name all production node operators.
Face Authentication compares a live phone-camera image to encrypted face images stored on the user's phone and is separate from the iris-MPC uniqueness path.
